issues.description: PR bundles three unrelated changes (tests, README reformat, FAQ addition) into one diff.
issues.detail: Stated scope is adding POST tests, but the diff also rewrites the README example (reformatting, handle() signature reorder, status formatting, bounded_stream swap) and adds an FAQ entry. Reviewing is harder because the test change is buried under noise. Split into separate PRs so each change can be justified on its own.

issues.description: Switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream is a silent semantic change.
issues.detail: The example swaps req.stream.read() for req.bounded_stream.read() with no comment, no versionchanged note, and a PR description that says something different ('add req.content_length to req.stream.read()'). The two streams behave differently when Content-Length is wrong or absent. Name the change, document why bounded_stream is correct, and align the commit message.

issues.description: README handle() signature reordered to (req, resp, ex, params) as an undocumented drive-by.
issues.detail: Original README used (ex, req, resp, params); the diff reorders to (req, resp, ex, params). Whether or not this matches current Falcon API, it is unmentioned in the commit message of a PR titled 'add POST request tests'. Either justify the change explicitly against the current add_error_handler contract or drop it from this PR.

issues.description: FAQ example handler is overcomplicated and obscures the lesson being taught.
issues.detail: PostTest.on_post layers nested if/else, double None-or-0 checks, and three status codes to demonstrate 'how to set headers in tests'. It also contains an unbounded read pattern readers will copy. Simplify to the smallest handler that demonstrates the point, flatten the branches, and state the bound or use bounded_stream.

issues.description: FAQ test uses parenthesized assert, a known Python footgun.
issues.detail: `assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400)` reads like a function call and trains readers toward the broken `assert(x, y)` tuple form which is always truthy. In canonical example code that teaches testing, write `assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400` without parentheses.

issues.description: New POST tests duplicate header dicts instead of composing from a shared base.
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 both hardcode identical Authorization and Content-Type entries. Pull common headers into a local base dict and merge per-case overrides so the meaningful difference (Content-Length: 1, empty body) is obvious. Also add a one-line comment naming the contract each assertion enforces.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the underlying test additions are useful but the PR is poorly scoped: it smuggles a README reformat (including a handle() signature reorder) and a new FAQ section into a change advertised as 'add POST tests'. The bounded_stream swap in the example is the actual semantic fix that makes the new test pass, yet it is unexplained and contradicts the PR description. The FAQ example is more elaborate than the lesson it teaches and contains a copy-paste footgun (parenthesized assert) plus an unbounded read pattern. Recommended action: split the PR, document the bounded_stream rationale, simplify the FAQ resource, and either justify or drop the README signature change.
